newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Mobutu shuffles army high command.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu shuffles army high command.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko has shaken up the army high command, naming a new commander of land forces, which are battling rebels in the country's east, state radio reported on Saturday.

General Mosala Modjandongo, commander of the Lower Zaire region, replaced General Mulumba Ambote, it said, quoting a presidential decree signed by Mobutu on February 17, before his departure for his villa in France on Friday.
The shake-up follows advances by rebels from the east on several fronts, blunting an army counter-offensive launched from Zaire's third city of Kisangani on January 20.

Defence officials contacted by Reuters on Saturday were unable to elaborate on the reasons for the latest change in the high command, which has seen its forces struggling against mainly Tutsi-led rebels who took up arms last October.
Mobutu, who had prostate surgery last August in Europe, returned to Zaire after four months absence and shuffled the army high command in December.

He appointed General Mahele Lieko Bokungo as armed forces chief of staff. Mahele is one of the few senior generals in Zaire who has earned his reputation on the battlefield and not through close family or ethnic ties to Mobutu.
A senior defence ministry official said earlier on Saturday that Zaire's armed forces had been using helicopter gunships to attack rebels advancing from the north and east on Kisangani.

"Since Wednesday our MI-24 combat helicopter have been conducting raids between Bafwasende and Banalia," the official told Reuters, adding that rebels had been as close as 130 km (80 miles) to the city. The raids continued on Friday.
Kisangani, strategically placed on the Zaire River, is headquarters for the army's counter-offensive and rebel leader Laurent Kabila has named it as one of his targets.
